question: What will Moderna (MRNA) stock close at on Friday, September 4, 2026?

For example, a closing price of $145.13 resolves as 145.13. If Yahoo Finance is unavailable, the closing price reported by another financial data provider such as Investing.com or MarketWatch, or by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions), will be used.
reference_class: One-trading-day-ahead close of a US large-cap stock (daily random walk anchored on the prior close), restricted to post-binary-event high-volatility biotech — names two-to-three weeks past a major clinical readout with realized annualized vol above 100%
dispersion_basis: post-event realized daily log-return SD Aug 21-Sep 3 (n=10) = 6.7%, blended toward the decaying last-5-day 4.5% to ~6.2%; 6.2% x 2.563 = 15.9% of 148.2 = 23.5, before a fat-tail widening to the declared 25.1 width
reasoning: One trading day remains. Sep 3 close is known: $148.87 (Yahoo historical page and stockanalysis.com both give it; -1.29% from Sep 2's $150.81, which the Benzinga Sep 3 piece independently confirms). The $144.54 in search snippets is an intraday quote (7.01M volume vs 40M average), not a close. A one-day-ahead close is close to a martingale, so the prior median is last close; I shaded it ~0.4% lower to $148.2 on the thin after-hours print ($147.75) and a mild bearish tilt: a fresh Rothschild Sell downgrade (PT $81), convert-arb short hedging from the $2.6-3.0B 2032 notes that closed Sep 1, and 4.81% 10Y yields pressuring long-duration growth. Offsetting: continued momentum from the Aug 19 intismeran Phase 3 readout, the mFLUSIVA approval, and the updated COVID formulation clearance. Width is set by realized post-shock vol (6.7% daily SD over Aug 21-Sep 3, decaying to ~4.5% in the last five sessions) against implied vol of 110-145% annualized (6.9-9.1%/day) — I sat nearer realized but widened the tails for this stock's demonstrated -23%/+14% daily capability. Fri Sep 4 carries the August jobs report (consensus +53k) with two-sided risk, and is a thin pre-Labor-Day session. No human market prices this: Polymarket has Moderna contracts (Merck acquisition, ~$17M volume) but none on a daily close, and I found no Kalshi MRNA range market.
what_would_change_my_mind: A verified Sep 3 close materially different from $148.87 (e.g. confirmation that $144.54 was the official close, not an intraday quote)
Material overnight Moderna-specific news: an acquisition approach, a regulatory action, or any question about the INTerpath-001 data
A large after-hours or pre-market move on real volume, or an S&P/index-rebalance announcement touching MRNA
A jobs-report surprise far outside consensus (+53k) that moves the whole long-duration growth complex several percent

question: What will the U.S. unemployment rate be for August 2026, as reported in the September 4, 2026 Employment Situation release?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves to the seasonally adjusted U.S. civilian unemployment rate (U-3) for August 2026, as reported by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics in the "Employment Situation" news release scheduled for Friday, September 4, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, published at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm . The value is the headline unemployment rate stated in the release summary (for example, a reported rate of 4.1 percent resolves as 4.1). Any subsequent revision to the August 2026 figure is ignored; the value as first published on September 4, 2026 governs.
reference_class: First-print month-over-month changes in the seasonally adjusted U.S. U-3 unemployment rate (unrounded, computed from CPS Table A-1 levels), 2023-2026 'low-hire, low-fire' regime, conditioned on the rounding position of the prior month
dispersion_basis: SD of month-over-month changes in the UNROUNDED SA U-3 computed from BLS Table A-1 levels (Mar-Jul 2026: +0.081, -0.041, -0.107, -0.099) and the wider 2023-2026 regime, ~0.115 pp, x 2.56
reasoning: Reference class first: in the 2023-2026 low-hire/low-fire regime the one-month change in unrounded U-3 is centered near zero with SD ~0.11pp, so the prior is 'prints the same as last month' (4.1). The decisive case fact is the rounding position: July unrounded was 4.090% (6,916/169,094, Table A-1), only -0.04 from a 4.0 print but +0.06 from a 4.2 print, and momentum is downward (three consecutive unrounded declines averaging -0.08/month) as the labor force contracts on retirements, restrictive immigration and the July 27 TPS revocation. Against that: Dow Jones consensus is +53k payrolls after -23k, continuing claims rose to 1.779M, Challenger August layoffs +58% m/m and the hiring rate fell to 3.2% — RSM explicitly says '4.1% with modest risk of an increase'. Kalshi's exact-match August contract (~30k OI, tightest book on the 4.3 strike) prices 4.1 at ~34% but 4.2 at ~31% and 4.0 at only ~15%; I blended roughly half-and-half with my own N(4.11, 0.115) latent model, keeping the market's 4.1 mode but moving mass from 4.2/4.3 toward 4.0 because retail flow appears to ignore the 4.090 anchor. Implied point masses: 3.9 ~6%, 4.0 ~20%, 4.1 ~34%, 4.2 ~27%, 4.3 ~11%, 4.4+ ~2%. Release is confirmed for Sep 4 08:30 ET with no shutdown risk reported.
what_would_change_my_mind: The August household survey showing the labor force expanding rather than contracting again (participation back up from 61.4%), which would break the mechanical driver of the recent decline and push the unrounded rate above 4.15
A large jump in the unrounded unemployed level (>150k) or payrolls printing materially negative, signalling the low-fire regime has cracked
Kalshi's 4.2/4.3 strikes bid up sharply into the print on real size, indicating informed flow I am discounting
Evidence that the TPS revocation moved 300k people into 'unemployed' rather than out of the labor force

question: What will the reported change in U.S. total nonfarm payroll employment be for August 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves to the seasonally adjusted change in total nonfarm payroll employment for August 2026, as first reported in the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics "Employment Situation" news release scheduled for 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time on Friday, September 4, 2026, available at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm . The value is expressed in thousands of jobs: for example, a reported increase of 75,000 jobs resolves as 75, and a decline of 40,000 jobs resolves as -40. Later revisions to the August 2026 figure do not affect resolution; only the value in the initial release counts.
reference_class: Monthly US total nonfarm payroll first prints (BLS establishment survey), 2026 cooling regime — trailing 3-month and 12-month averages plus the distribution of first-print-minus-consensus surprises 2022-2026
dispersion_basis: BLS's own stated 90% CI for the monthly change in total nonfarm employment is about ±122k, implying a sampling SD ≈74k that is irreducible for any forecaster; historical first-print-minus-consensus SD has run ~65-80k in 2022-2026. 74 x 2.563 ≈ 190, and I widen slightly for TPS-timing uncertainty; declared width 200.
reasoning: Reference class: monthly US nonfarm payroll first prints in the 2026 cooling regime (3-mo avg +20k, 12-mo avg +34k, July -23k), which anchors ~+25k before news. Dow Jones consensus is +53k, i.e. it prices a rebound ABOVE trend in a month carrying a large one-off labor-supply shock: Haiti TPS terminated 2026-07-27, ~200k valid work permits, first landing in the August reference period (pay period incl. Aug 12) and invisible to jobless claims since these workers are benefit-ineligible. Named forecasts span -25k to +90k, an unusually wide band that is itself a dispersion signal. Consensus and prediction markets both overshot in June and July, so I shade below both: Kalshi implies median ~+50k (50% >50k, 25% <0, 25% >80k) and Polymarket's thin $31k book implies ~+40k. Offsetting the bearish case: Challenger layoffs were the slowest August since 2022, claims sit at 206k inside a narrow 2026 band, and first prints in this low-response-rate era run high relative to later revisions - so the TPS drag may show up in revisions rather than Friday's headline. Net: median +28k, left-skewed, with the 10-90 width held at the BLS-implied noise floor rather than tuned narrower.
what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence that Haitian TPS terminations were largely deferred, litigated, or absorbed via replacement hiring before the Aug 12 reference period
A Kalshi/Polymarket repricing on Sept 3-4 that moves the implied median well away from ~+40-50k on volume
Confirmation that BLS's August seasonal factors or birth-death model were revised in a way that shifts the print systematically
Late-breaking August state-level or industry data (healthcare/hospitality employment) showing a discrete August drop

question: What will the August 2026 seasonally adjusted change in U.S. government employment be, per the BLS report?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves to the seasonally adjusted over-the-month change in total "Government" employment for August 2026 (i.e., the July 2026 to August 2026 change), in thousands, as shown in Table B-1 of the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics "Employment Situation" news release scheduled for release on September 4, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.t17.htm). The value is computed as the August 2026 seasonally adjusted Government employment level minus the July 2026 seasonally adjusted Government employment level, both from the "Government" total line of Table B-1, expressed in thousands. For example, a decline of 53,000 jobs resolves as -53, and a gain of 12,000 jobs resolves as 12.
reference_class: Monthly SA over-the-month changes in total U.S. government payrolls (BLS CES) during the 2026 contraction regime (Jan-Jul 2026, n=7), with August-specific dispersion taken from August prints 2016-2025 excluding pandemic 2020
dispersion_basis: component SD build-up: local gov education ~30 (its own 2017-2025 August SD in non-pandemic years, haircut for the lower-variance 2026 regime) plus federal/state/local-ex-ed ~8 each and ~8 for the July revision that moves the base, giving SD ~31; x 2.56
reasoning: Reference-class anchor: 2026 monthly SA government prints average -11k, with federal now near-flat and the entire drag in local government education. August is the highest-variance month in this series because the seasonal factor absorbs a ~1M gross school-hiring swing. Two forces pull opposite ways. Mean reversion: July's -49.6 in local gov education is the second-largest July drop on record, Jul->Aug correlation in that series is about -0.46, and the closest analogue (2018, -44.5 -> +28.7) fully reversed; CEPR/EPI-style reads call July an artifact of districts releasing summer staff ~5% above norm. Structural: local gov education has fallen four straight months on widening district deficits, ESSER expiry and enrollment decline, with the biggest school layoff wave in a decade taking effect precisely in the August-September reference periods, and RSM forecasts a third consecutive negative government print. I land modestly negative, near the 2026 trend rather than near the -53 outlier or a full reversal to positive. That is also roughly what the +53k headline consensus embeds against ADP private +38k. Left tail is fatter than the right: a school-hiring shortfall against a million-job gross swing produced -64 in August 2017 in a far more benign regime, while a >+50 print needs a full artifact reversal that the underlying downtrend argues against. Escape masses: 5% above +50 (clean, complete reversal of the July artifact on top of state-university timing, as in 2019's +53); 1.5% below -130, which needs an Oct-2025-style mass federal separation event -- the OPM deferred-resignation cohort goes on PAID administrative leave from end-August, so it stays on payroll and does not supply that mechanism.
what_would_change_my_mind: An upward revision to July 2026 local government education in the August report (raising the base and mechanically pushing the August change more negative)
Evidence that August school-start dates in 2026 shifted materially earlier or later than the seasonal factor assumes
State government education showing another 2025-style August drop (-12.7) on university-calendar timing
A new federal RIF or separation wave with an actual August effective date rather than paid administrative leave
A headline NFP print far from the +53k consensus with a known private-sector split

Five lenses: (1) pure random walk from 0.69; (2) post-blow-off fade -- the stock peaked at 0.90 on Sep 1, fell 21% then 2.8%, and closed Sep 3 at its session low of 0.68, a mildly bearish tape signal; (3) squeeze-continuation -- R$45mn daily turnover on a R$67mn market cap, retail momentum, and live RJ/DIP headline catalysts keep a fat right tail; (4) fundamentals -- equity behind R$17.3bn of RJ debt and a R$10.1bn quarterly loss is close to worthless, a persistent negative drift; (5) analogs (Americanas, Oi, Light after RJ filings) -- post-filing squeezes fade over weeks but day-to-day direction is near-coin-flip. question: How many named storms will the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season have had by September 5, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question asks for the cumulative number of named tropical storms in the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season that had formed on or before September 5, 2026 (i.e. that were assigned a name from the Atlantic naming list at any point through that date). It resolves based on the National Hurricane Center's 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Season summary table at https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/index.php?season=2026&basin=atl — specifically, the count of distinct named systems (those listed with a name such as Arthur, Bertha, etc.) whose first attainment of tropical-storm or subtropical-storm status (the start of the "Dates active" range) fell on or before September 5, 2026 (UTC). A system is counted if it was named on or before September 5, 2026, regardless of its later intensity (a system that strengthened into a hurricane still counts as one named storm). For example, if six named systems had formed through September 5, the question resolves as 6.
reference_class: Strong-El Nino Atlantic hurricane seasons (1982, 1987, 1991, 1997, 2002, 2009, 2015): cumulative named storms formed by September 5
dispersion_basis: Both the 10th and 90th percentile outcomes are 5 named storms (zero additional formations in the remaining ~49h), so true count dispersion is ~0; 0.5 count-units declared as a conservative floor covering the ~1.5% tail at 6.
reasoning: Prior from the reference class of strong-El Nino Atlantic seasons' cumulative named-storm count by Sep 5 (1982, 1987, 1991, 1997, 2002, 2009, 2015): median ~5. The observed 2026 count is exactly 5 (Arthur, Bertha, Cristobal, Dolly, Edouard, per Wikipedia and NHC), and the fine print forbids counting unnamed depressions or post-resolution reclassification, so 5 is a hard floor and the only live question is whether a 6th (Fay) is named by end of Sep 5 UTC. The NHC 18:00Z Sep 3 Tropical Weather Outlook states formation is not expected during the next 7 days, with no invests or shaded areas anywhere in the basin. Climatologically a 2-day window in early September contains a genesis ~25-35% of the time, but that base rate is conditioned away by an explicit zero-percent NHC outlook: false negatives at 1-2 day lead after such an issuance run ~1%, and a very strong El Nino shear regime that has produced zero hurricanes (nearing the satellite-era record) argues lower still. I put ~1.5% on 6 and negligible mass above, EV 5.02. Market check: no contract matching this threshold/deadline/source found on Kalshi or Polymarket, so no crowd anchor was applied.

question: How many waterbodies will be on the Massachusetts DPH harmful cyanobacterial bloom advisory list on September 4, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves as the number of distinct waterbodies listed under the "Current List of Waterbodies" section of the Massachusetts Department of Public Health "Harmful Cyanobacterial Bloom Advisories in Massachusetts" page (https://www.mass.gov/info-details/harmful-cyanobacterial-bloom-advisories-in-massachusetts) on the version of the page that is "current as of" a date falling on or after August 31, 2026 and on or before September 4, 2026. Each bulleted waterbody entry counts as one, exactly as the page enumerates them (for example, the version current as of August 21, 2026 listed 25 entries, which would resolve as 25). If multiple dated versions qualify, use the one whose "current as of" date is closest to and not after September 4, 2026.
reference_class: Late-August / early-September editions of the Massachusetts DPH statewide cyanobacteria advisory list (2025 and 2026 bloom seasons), plus the general class of 'already-published government list snapshots read within days of posting'
dispersion_basis: ~74% point mass on the already-posted Sept-1 version (31 entries, verified twice on the live page); ~26% branch of a Sept-3/4 repost whose 0-3 day count change has SD ~3 (2026: 25 on Aug 21 -> 31 on Sep 1, ~+0.55/day; 2025: ~27 early Aug -> ~40 early Sep); plus ~10% chance my proxy extraction miscounts the bullets by +/-1
reasoning: Direct observation dominates: the live DPH page reads 'current as of September 1, 2026' with 31 bulleted waterbodies, and mass.gov's algae index shows it was updated Sep 1, 2026 4:00 pm. That version already falls inside the Aug 31-Sep 4 qualifying window, so 31 is the default answer. The only path to a different number is a fresh version dated Sep 2-4 posted before Sep 5 00:00 UTC (Sep 4, 8 pm ET); as of 2026-09-03 22:50 UTC no Sep 2 or Sep 3 version has appeared, leaving roughly one Friday business day. Weighing a ~7-day update cadence in 2026 (Aug 21 -> Sep 1) against 2025's much faster peak-season cadence and a plausible pre-Labor-Day refresh, I put ~30% on a new qualifying version; conditional on one, the count is centered ~32 (rising trend, offset by advisories being lifted) with SD ~3. Mass.gov 2026 dated archive pages do not exist under the 2025 URL pattern (probe 404d), so intermediate 2026 versions could not be enumerated - cadence evidence is thinner than I would like, which is why I keep meaningful mass off 31 rather than collapsing to it. No human prediction market prices this (searched Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold): none found. No mechanism gets the list from 31 to 46+ in three days, so no upper-escape mass is declared.
what_would_change_my_mind: The DPH page's 'current as of' line changing to September 3 or 4, 2026 before Sep 4 8 pm ET (would shift the distribution to the new count and widen it)
Evidence that DPH posted intermediate 2026 versions between Aug 21 and Sep 1 (implying a sub-weekly cadence and a much higher chance of a Sep 4 repost)
A direct un-proxied read of the page returning a bullet count other than 31
A DPH statement of a fixed weekly update day, especially if that day is Friday

question: How many of the four vessels held by Somali pirates (HONOUR 25, SWARD, EUREKA, ASANA) will still be under pirate control on September 5, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves as the number of the following four merchant vessels — HONOUR 25 (Palau-flagged product tanker), SWARD (Saint Kitts and Nevis-flagged cargo vessel), EUREKA (Togo-flagged tanker), and ASANA (Tanzania-flagged tanker, also rendered ASNA) — that remain under Somali pirate control as of September 5, 2026, according to EU NAVFOR Operation Atalanta. A vessel is counted as still under pirate control if, as of September 5, 2026, Atalanta has NOT publicly announced its release/liberation (or the release of its crew) via its newsroom (https://www.eunavfor.eu/news) or official social media. A vessel is counted as released (and therefore NOT included in the total) once Atalanta reports the ship and/or its crew have been freed, whether by ransom, naval action, negotiation, or any other means. For example, if Atalanta has announced the release of EUREKA but the other three remain held, this resolves as 3. If Atalanta's newsroom is unavailable, resolution may rely on credible sources (https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting Atalanta's status of these vessels.
reference_class: Somali ransom hijackings of merchant vessels (2008-2026) still under pirate control more than one month after seizure, evaluated over a fixed ~1-day window
dispersion_basis: ~96% point mass on the outcome 4 implies a within-bin (3.5-4.5) uniform spread of ~0.84 units; the underlying count has not changed at all over any 1-day window since 17 July, so bin width, not real variance, sets the floor
reasoning: Reference class: Somali ransom hijackings still held after >1 month have a daily release-announcement hazard of roughly 1%/vessel-day (historical durations run months to years; median well past the 4.5 months HONOUR 25 has already run). Over a ~25-hour window with 4 vessels that gives ~4% chance at least one release is announced, so EV ~3.96 and P(count=4) ~0.96. Evidence pushes if anything lower: Atalanta's last update (29 Jul) still lists all four; Sept 3 Egyptian reporting has EUREKA's talks stalled with the demand raised to $10M; Pakistan says it is barred from paying ransom for HONOUR 25 and reports zero negotiation progress; nothing at all on SWARD or ASANA. Resolution also requires a public Atalanta announcement by 5 Sep 00:00Z, and Atalanta's newsroom cadence is weeks-long, so even a Friday release might not be announced in time. Counterweight: Turkey's ~10-day kinetic rescue of the Lutuf in August shows naval action is live, multiple flag states are under domestic pressure, and a coordinated deal could free more than one at once — but the four sit anchored inside Somali territorial waters close to shore with 67 hostages, which Atalanta explicitly cites as constraining action. Thin, one-sided evidence, so I stay near the status-quo anchor. No human market exists on this.

question: Will WHO or Africa CDC report more than 10,000 people vaccinated with Ervebo in the 2026 DRC Bundibugyo Ebola response before September 4, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if, before 23:59 UTC on September 3, 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) or the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) publishes a report stating that more than 10,000 people have cumulatively received the Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV-GP) vaccine as part of the response to the 2026 Ebola disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo caused by Bundibugyo virus (declared 15 May 2026). Eligible publications include WHO Disease Outbreak News (https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news), WHO Regional Office for Africa outbreak bulletins, and Africa CDC situation reports/dashboards. The figure must refer to people vaccinated (or doses administered, since Ervebo is a single-dose vaccine), not doses allocated, released, delivered, or pre-positioned. It resolves NO if no such report puts the cumulative figure above 10,000 by that time.
reference_class: Ebola vaccination ring/frontline campaigns in DRC, ~1 week after first injection, with a specific cumulative-vaccinated figure published by WHO/Africa CDC
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent runs [0.01, 0.02, 0.02] -> 0.016; the narrative below is the research run's own view (0.01)]
Direct instrument read, not a base-rate extrapolation. Africa CDC's own briefing (Wessam Mankoula, reported by Xinhua 4 Sep) put cumulative vaccinated at 1,124 healthcare/frontline workers as of 1 September 2026 — the campaign started 27 Aug under compassionate use in Tshopo, giving a pace near 200-250/day. Reaching >10,000 by 3 Sep would require ~4,500/day, roughly 20x the observed rate, AND a single WHO or Africa CDC publication stating it within the ~1 hour remaining to the 23:59 UTC deadline. WHO's own 1 Sep emergency guidance restricts Ervebo here to trial/compassionate protocols, and WHO said on 2-3 Sep that efficacy trials only begin Oct-Nov, so the 20,000 trial doses are not being administered yet. Only ~16,250-50,000 doses had even arrived; delivered/allocated figures are explicitly excluded by the fine print. No human market prices this (Polymarket has only 'Ebola pandemic in 2026' at ~7.5%, a different contract on WHO's use of the word 'pandemic' — not an anchor). Residual probability covers only a late-breaking bulletin with a figure inconsistent with everything published so far.
what_would_change_my_mind: A WHO AFRO bulletin or Africa CDC situation report published 2-3 Sep 2026 giving a cumulative vaccinated figure above 10,000
Evidence that the 1,124 figure was a subset (e.g. one province) and a national total an order of magnitude higher exists in an official publication
Confirmation that a mass preventive campaign beyond frontline workers had already been running for weeks with its own count

missing_evidence: No direct read of a WHO AFRO weekly bulletin or Africa CDC dashboard dated 2-3 Sep 2026; my checks returned no such document carrying vaccination counts, but absence-of-evidence here rests on search coverage rather than confirmed inspection of every eligible source.
No visibility into any Africa CDC situation report or WHO AFRO bulletin actually published 2-3 Sep 2026; the 1,124 figure is from a wire report of a briefing, not a primary document I retrieved.

question: Will the FAA authorize SpaceX's Starship reentry trajectory to Starbase before September 4, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if, as of September 4, 2026 (00:00 UTC), the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued a modification to SpaceX's Starship/Super Heavy vehicle operator license (License No. VOL 23-129) that authorizes an additional Starship reentry/landing trajectory returning to the Boca Chica (Starbase, Texas) launch site — the regulatory step required for a Mechazilla tower catch of the Starship upper stage. Any such license modification issued and still in effect at any time before September 4, 2026 (00:00 UTC) counts. It resolves NO otherwise. Resolution is based on the FAA's SpaceX Starship stakeholder page (https://www.faa.gov/space/stakeholder_engagement/spacex_starship) showing an issued license modification (not merely a completed environmental review), or on confirmation from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) that the FAA has granted such a license modification.
reference_class: FAA Starship NEPA completions (FONSI/ROD) and the interval to the corresponding issued vehicle-operator-license modification — specifically, the fraction issued within one day of the ROD
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent runs [0.12, 0.09, 0.07] -> 0.091; the narrative below is the research run's own view (0.12)]
The FAA action that landed on 2026-09-03 was the Final Tiered EA with FONSI/ROD covering the additional Boca Chica reentry trajectory and expanded Pacific contingency areas — reported by enthusiast outlets as 'FAA approves the landing catch,' and by one search summary explicitly as 'the approval came from the FAA's Final Tiered Environmental Assessment.' The fine print carves this out: NEPA completion alone does not count; an issued modification to VOL 23-129 is required. Precedent strongly separates the two steps: the Feb 17, 2026 FONSI/ROD for 'Additional Launch Trajectories and Starship Boca Chica Landings' was followed by no issued license modification through late August 2026 (~6 months), and the May 2025 analogue lagged ~9 days. TechTimes on Sept 2 still headlined 'FAA Approval Remains.' I could not open the FAA stakeholder page (403), so a concurrently issued license modification not yet reflected in secondary reporting is the main YES path, alongside resolver conflation of the headline with the licensing step. Urgency is also reduced because Flight 14 (NET Sept 15) is reported per the Aug 31 FCC filing as an Indian Ocean splashdown, with the catch pushed to a later flight.
what_would_change_my_mind: The FAA SpaceX Starship stakeholder page's licensing section showing a VOL 23-129 revision dated on or before 2026-09-03 that names a Starbase reentry/landing trajectory
An FAA statement or a tier-1 outlet (SpaceNews, NASASpaceflight, Ars, Spaceflight Now, Reuters) reporting an issued license modification, not an environmental finding, before 2026-09-04 00:00 UTC
A new VOL 23-129 revision PDF appearing on faa.gov or DRS with a September 2026 date

missing_evidence: Direct read of the FAA SpaceX Starship stakeholder page and its activity archive (HTTP 403 to automated fetch) and of any September 2026 VOL 23-129 revision in DRS; the Sept 3 FAA email text is known only through an enthusiast blog's paraphrase.

['Direct read of https://www.faa.gov/space/stakeholder_engagement/spacex_starship (403 to automated fetch) — the named resolution source', 'The full text of the Sept 3 FAA email/announcement to confirm whether it covered only NEPA or also the license action']

question: What will be the cumulative net flow into US spot Bitcoin ETFs over September 1–4, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves based on the "Total" row of the US Bitcoin ETF flow table published by Farside Investors at https://farside.co.uk/btc/ . It resolves as the sum of the daily "Total" net flow values (in US$ millions) reported for the four trading days 1, 2, 3, and 4 September 2026, expressed in millions of US dollars. For example, if the four daily totals are +150.0, -50.0, +200.0, and +100.0, the sum is +400.0 and the question resolves as 400. Positive values denote net inflows and negative values denote net outflows. If Farside does not report a value for a given day (e.g. a market holiday), that day contributes 0. If Farside Investors is permanently unavailable, an equivalent aggregate from another public US spot Bitcoin ETF flow tracker (e.g. SoSoValue) covering the same four days will be used.
reference_class: Rolling four-trading-day cumulative Farside 'Total' net-flow sums for US spot Bitcoin ETFs during 2026, conditioned on the first two days of this window being already known (-236.5 and +101.1)
dispersion_basis: SD of daily Farside Total across the 21 August 2026 sessions = 210; two unknown days with mild positive autocorrelation gives a 2-day-sum SD of ~340; 340 x 2.56 = 870
reasoning: Two of the four days are already published and fix 2 of 4 terms: Sept 1 = -236.5 (largest outflow since July 31, IBIT -201.2) and Sept 2 = +101.1, so MTD = -135.4. Only Sept 3 (session closed but unpublished as of 23:05 UTC) and Sept 4 remain. Reference class is rolling 4-trading-day Farside Total sums in 2026; August 2026 averaged +168/day (SD 210, range -201.8 to +606.3) but that was the strongest month of the year, and the 2026 full-year pace is closer to +85/day. Price action is choppy rather than trending - BTC fell to ~$76.4k on Sept 3 before recovering, after a -1.3% week - which argues for modest creations, so I centre the two remaining days near +80/day rather than August's +168. Draws under five framings (August-mean continuation, September-regime softness, price-action-conditioned, pre-Labor-Day/NFP risk-off Friday, 2026 full-year mean) gave +200, -75, +40, -115, +35; median +35, and I shade to +25 for the soft Sept 3 tape. No human prediction market prices this contract (Kalshi/Polymarket cover BTC price windows only), so no crowd blend. Sept 4 is the first Friday (August NFP) and precedes Labor Day, a catalyst that widens the spread rather than moving the centre. Escape mass is small: -1000 needs two ~-430 days (BTC-record territory, ~2%); +2000 needs two ~+1070 days, unprecedented back-to-back and inconsistent with the current tone (~1%).

question: What will the most recent WHO Disease Outbreak News report as the cumulative confirmed Ebola deaths in the DRC, as of September 4, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves to the number of cumulative confirmed deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reported in the most recently published WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) item concerning the ongoing Ebola disease outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus, as that item appears on the WHO Disease Outbreak News repository (https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news) as of 23:59 UTC on September 3, 2026. The figure used is the cumulative number of confirmed deaths in the DRC (not the multi-country outbreak total, and not probable/suspected deaths). For example, if the latest DON states "4,665 confirmed cases and 2,184 deaths" in the DRC, this resolves as 2184.
reference_class: WHO Disease Outbreak News publication cadence for the 2026 DRC Bundibugyo outbreak (DONs of 16 May, 8 Jun, ~5 Aug, 14 Aug, 28 Aug — 9 to 14 day gaps), combined with the standing figure in the most recent such item
dispersion_basis: Outcome is an already-published figure read directly from the resolution source (DON616, 28 Aug 2026 = 2786), so ~95% of mass sits on one point; the 10-90 width is driven entirely by scenario risk, not series volatility — ~4-5% that an unindexed newer DON exists (it would report ~2,950-3,040, tracking national confirmed data with a ~2-day lag) plus ~1% fine-print fallback to the 14 Aug DON figure of 2,184.
reasoning: This question is effectively already resolved. WHO DON 2026-DON616, published 28 August 2026, states 5,794 confirmed cases including 2,786 deaths in the DRC as of 26 August (CFR 48.1%); the separate multi-country line gives 5,815 cases / 2,788 deaths including two in Uganda, confirming 2,786 is the DRC-only confirmed figure the criteria specify. Prior: the reference class of DON publication gaps for this outbreak (16 May, 8 Jun, ~5 Aug, 14 Aug, 28 Aug) is 9-14 days, so a fresh DON within 6 days would be faster than any gap seen. Direct check: 2026-DON617 and 2026-DON618 both 404 while 2026-DON615 resolves correctly and matches the known 14 Aug figures (4,665/2,184), so WHO has published no DON of any disease since 28 August. Counterargument: national surveillance has raced ahead (6,250 cases / 3,039 deaths as of 1 Sept per ECDC) and WHO messaging on 1-2 Sept was urgent, which could trigger an off-cadence DON — but nothing was published as of the resolution instant, and ~50 minutes remain. No human prediction market prices this contract (Polymarket's Ebola markets are on pandemic declaration and country case counts, different resolution sources and thresholds).
what_would_change_my_mind: A WHO DON on this outbreak with a publication date of 29 Aug-3 Sept 2026 appearing on the DON repository (would move the answer to roughly 2,950-3,040)
DON616's DRC death figure turning out to be a combined confirmed-and-probable count with no standalone confirmed number, triggering the fallback to 2,184
A revision or correction to DON616 restating the 26 August DRC confirmed-death total
